title: Unit – 5 : Session – 11 : SLO – 1  |  Memory-Mapped vs Port-Mapped I/O
sections: 1. B) Memory locations — MMIO treats device registers as memory addresses.
2. B) x86 CISC — port-mapped (isolated) I/O is characteristic of x86.
3. C) IN/OUT — the special instructions used for port-mapped I/O.
1. memory — MMIO shares its address space with main memory.
2. IN/OUT — PMIO uses special instructions such as IN and OUT.
3. RISC — MMIO is commonly used in RISC processors (ARM, MIPS).
1. TRUE — MMIO uses ordinary LOAD/STORE instructions.
2. FALSE — PMIO has a separate port address space.
2. 50 — the polling loop checks the status 50 times.
